_note: Paño's base brain: neutral wording for every line his engine (pano.js) and his four everyday skills (tours, background, windows, bin) say. Any brain can build on it with "extends": "base". Its own lines win, key by key, so a site only writes the lines it wants to change. {cat_name} is filled in with lines.name. In tour.step, {n}, {total} and {name} (the tour's name) are filled in by the engine. Only <b> and <span> tags are used.

lines.name: Paño
lines.hello: Hi, I’m {cat_name}! I can show you around. What would you like to do?

menu.ask: What would you like to do?
menu.after_tour: Done! What would you like to do next?
menu.lost: Hmm, I lost track of that. What would you like to do?
menu.bye: Okay! I’m right here if you need a hand.

tour._memory_note: The lines below are only said where the page gives him a memory (adapter entry "memory").
tour.intro: Each tour is short, and you can stop any time.
tour.next_up: Next up: {name}. Want to see it?
tour.next_talk: You’ve seen them all! Want to chat about {title}?
tour.im_good_bye: Okay! I’m right here if you need me.

touch._note: On touch screens these swaps are applied, in order, to every tour line. whole_word swaps the word wherever it stands alone.

background._note: options: the site's own words for each of its backgrounds, keyed by the names in its adapter. modes: the colorblind modes. note: an extra line he says after a colorblind mode is applied; leave it empty to skip it.
background.ask_mode: Which colorblind mode should I apply to the site?
background.changing: Okay, I am changing the background now for you.

cleanup.offer: You have a lot of windows open. Can I tidy them up?
cleanup.cleaned: All clean! I kept the one you were looking at.

bin.refuse: Excuse me. I am not recyclable.
